record.original_question: Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is W_{2k+2}-free, where W_{2k+2} is the even wheel on 2k+2 vertices, must lambda(G) be at most sqrt(4m/3), with equality only for regular complete 3-partite graphs?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.5 (Yu, Li and Peng [42], 2025). Let k >= 2 be fixed and m be large enough. If G in G(m, W2k+2), then lambda(G) <= sqrt(4m/3). Equality holds if and only if G is a regular complete 3-partite graph.
Consequently, Conjectures 4.3 and 4.5 are resolved completely.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a simple graph with m edges, and let λ(G) denote the spectral radius (largest eigenvalue) of its adjacency matrix. For an integer n ≥ 4, the wheel W_n on n vertices is the graph obtained by joining a single vertex (the hub) to every vertex of a cycle C_{n-1} on n-1 vertices; W_n is called an even wheel when n is even. A graph is said to be H-free if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to H.

Fix an integer k ≥ 2. Prove or disprove: there exists m_0 = m_0(k) such that for every m ≥ m_0, if G is a W_{2k+2}-free graph with m edges, then
    λ(G) ≤ √(4m/3),
with equality if and only if G is a regular complete 3-partite graph (i.e., a complete tripartite graph K_{t,t,t} for some positive integer t with 3t² = m·... such that m matches; equivalently, equality holds precisely when G is K_{t,t,t} for some t ≥ 1).
artifact.status_search_result: A recent survey on edge-spectral-Turán type problems states that this conjecture (along with a related one) has been "resolved completely." The parser metadata also marks the question as solved. Direct independent verification of the resolving paper was not located in the search, but the survey claim supports a solved status.

status_evidence.title: Survey on edge-spectral Turán problems (arXiv:2512.19395)
status_evidence.snippet: Consequently, Conjectures 4.3 and 4.5 are resolved completely.
status_evidence.claim: The even-wheel spectral conjecture of Yu, Li and Peng (2025) is reported as completely resolved.

status_evidence.title: Unsolved Problems in Spectral Graph Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Spectral Turán-type problems for forbidden subgraphs including wheels.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture sits within the spectral Turán framework of bounding λ(G) under forbidden-subgraph conditions on the number of edges.
